name: HSR Sync Failure After Takeover
description: HANA System Replication sync state does not reach SOK after a planned or unplanned takeover. The secondary shows SFAIL or SYNCING for an extended period.
symptoms: SAPHanaSR show returns SFAIL on secondary
systemReplicationStatus shows ERROR on secondary site
Indexserver trace shows reconnection errors
nameserver trace shows registration timeout
investigation: Check SAPHanaSR show or SAPHanaSR-angi show for current sync state
Run hdbnsutil -sr_state on both sites
Verify network connectivity between primary and secondary
Check HANA trace files for replication errors
Verify that AUTOMATED_REGISTER and PREFER_SITE_TAKEOVER are set to true in CIB
root_cause: HSR replication link not re-established after takeover due to registration failure or network partition.
fixes: Re-register secondary site: hdbnsutil -sr_register --remoteHost=<primary>
Verify and fix network routes between sites
Check and adjust HANA global.ini replication parameters
If SAPHanaSR-angi: verify susChkSrv.py hook is active

name: Fencing Not Triggered During Node Failure
description: Pacemaker detects a node failure but STONITH/fencing is not executed, leaving the cluster in a split-brain vulnerable state.
symptoms: Corosync reports node lost but no STONITH action in logs
crm_mon shows node as UNCLEAN
Pacemaker logs show no fencing attempts
SBD watchdog not triggered
investigation: Check stonith-enabled property in CIB
Verify SBD devices are accessible from all nodes
Check /var/log/messages for SBD and corosync entries
Run sbd -d <device> list to verify SBD slot status
Check Azure fence agent configuration if using AFA
root_cause: STONITH is misconfigured, disabled, or the fencing device is unreachable.
fixes: Enable stonith: crm configure property stonith-enabled=true
Verify SBD device connectivity and repair if needed
Check Azure fence agent credentials and API access
Ensure stonith-action is set to reboot

name: ANF Volume Throttling During Backup
description: Azure NetApp Files volume hits throughput or IOPS limits during HANA backup, causing backup failures or extreme slowness.
symptoms: HANA backup log shows timeout errors
ANF metrics show throttling events
iostat shows high await times on NFS mounts
Backup duration exceeds SLA threshold
investigation: Check ANF volume performance tier and throughput limits
Review HANA backup configuration for parallelism
Check Azure Monitor metrics for ANF throttling events
Verify NFS mount options (rsize, wsize, hard, noresvport)
root_cause: ANF volume throughput or IOPS limits exceeded during peak backup I/O.
fixes: Upgrade ANF volume to higher performance tier (Ultra)
Reduce backup parallelism to stay within limits
Schedule backups during low-activity periods
Split backup across multiple ANF volumes

name: Enqueue Replication Server Failover Failure
description: ENSA2 enqueue replication server (ERS) does not take over the enqueue lock table after ASCS node failure, causing SAP application downtime.
symptoms: SAP application servers report enqueue connection lost
sapcontrol -function GetProcessList shows enq_replicator stopped
Pacemaker shows ERS resource in stopped state
Enqueue lock table lost after failover
investigation: Check ERS process status with sapcontrol
Verify ENSA1 vs ENSA2 configuration
Check Pacemaker resource constraints and colocation rules
Review /var/log/messages for resource agent errors
Verify enqueue replication profile parameters
root_cause: ERS resource agent failed to start or the replication profile is misconfigured.
fixes: Fix ERS resource agent configuration in CIB
Verify enqueue replication profile (enque/replication_port, etc.)
Restart ERS resource: crm resource restart <ers_resource>
Check and update SAP kernel patches for ENSA2 fixes

name: Network Isolation Causes Split Brain
description: Loss of network connectivity between cluster nodes without proper fencing leads to a potential split-brain scenario where both nodes think they are primary.
symptoms: Both nodes report SOK as primary in SAPHanaSR show
Corosync ring marked faulty
No STONITH action despite node communication loss
Application connects to wrong primary
investigation: Check corosync ring status on both nodes
Verify network redundancy (bonding, multiple rings)
Check iptables/firewall rules for blocked ports
Review Azure NSG rules for inter-node communication
Verify SBD or Azure fence agent can reach nodes via out-of-band path
root_cause: Network partition without functional fencing allows both nodes to assume primary role.
fixes: Restore network connectivity between nodes
Ensure fencing is properly configured and tested
Configure corosync with redundant rings
Add Azure internal load balancer health probe
Test fencing regularly with crm node fence <node>

name: SAP Command Execution User Context
description: SAP HANA and SAP application commands must be run as the correct OS user. Most HANA tools (HDB, hdbnsutil, hdbuserstore, python replication scripts) require the <sid>adm user. Pacemaker and OS commands run as root. Failure to use the correct user results in 'command not found' or permission errors.
symptoms: sudo: HDB: command not found
hdbnsutil: command not found
Permission denied when running SAP commands
sapcontrol returns error accessing instance profile
python systemReplicationStatus.py fails with import error
investigation: Identify the SAP SID from workspace metadata or crm_mon output
Determine instance number from resource names (e.g. rsc_SAPHana_R11_HDB00 means SID=R11, NR=00)
Check if the command is an SAP tool or an OS tool
root_cause: SAP utilities are installed under /usr/sap/<SID> and are only in PATH for the <sid>adm user. Running them as root fails because root does not have the SAP environment variables sourced.
fixes: Use su - <sid>adm -c '<command>' to run SAP commands (e.g. su - r11adm -c 'HDB info')
Use su - <sid>adm -c 'hdbnsutil -sr_state' for replication state
Use su - <sid>adm -c 'python /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/exe/python_support/systemReplicationStatus.py' for replication status
sapcontrol can run as root if you use the full path: /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/exe/sapcontrol -nr <NR> -function GetProcessList
SAPHanaSR-showAttr and crm_mon work as root — no su needed
The SID is always UPPERCASE in paths (e.g. /usr/sap/R11) but lowercase in the adm user (e.g. r11adm)

name: Log File Investigation for HA Triage
description: When investigating HA cluster failures, test failures, or SAP issues, always check relevant log files for error messages, timestamps, and root cause indicators. Logs provide the ground truth for what happened and when. Combine log evidence with cluster state evidence for a complete picture.
symptoms: Test case failed with unclear error
Cluster resource failover occurred
HANA takeover happened unexpectedly
Fencing or STONITH was triggered
Node rebooted or went offline
SCS/ERS failover failed or was delayed
Application connectivity lost during failover
investigation: Check Pacemaker logs for resource agent actions and errors: tail -100 /var/log/pacemaker/pacemaker.log
Check system messages for cluster events, fencing, and SBD: tail -200 /var/log/messages
Check Corosync logs for ring failures and quorum changes: grep -i 'corosync\|quorum' /var/log/messages | tail -50
Check HANA nameserver trace for takeover/failover events: su - <sid>adm -c 'tail -100 /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/$(hostname)/trace/nameserver_*.trc'
Check HANA alert trace for critical errors: su - <sid>adm -c 'tail -50 /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/$(hostname)/trace/nameserver_alert_$(hostname).trc'
Check SBD logs for watchdog and disk heartbeat events: grep -i sbd /var/log/messages | tail -30
Use journalctl for recent systemd events: journalctl -u pacemaker --since '1 hour ago' --no-pager | tail -50
Check HANA system replication log shipping state in trace: su - <sid>adm -c 'grep -i "replication\|shipped\|replay" /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/$(hostname)/trace/nameserver_*.trc | tail -30'
Check sapstartsrv and sapcontrol logs for SCS/ERS issues: tail -50 /usr/sap/<SID>/ASCS<NR>/work/sapstartsrv.log
root_cause: Log files contain the definitive sequence of events during any cluster operation. Skipping log investigation leads to speculative conclusions.
fixes: Always include log evidence alongside cluster state when reporting findings
Correlate timestamps across multiple log sources (Pacemaker, corosync, HANA trace, syslog)
Look for the first error in the chain — subsequent errors are often cascading effects
If logs are too large, use time-range filtering: grep with timestamp patterns or journalctl --since/--until

name: TrexNet Erroneous SSL Channel on HANA Internal Ports
description: HANA nameserver alert trace shows 'erroneous SSL channel' and 'new Request with no or invalid request begin identifier' errors on internal ports (30001-30007, 40001-40007). These appear as TrexNet/TrexNetBuffer error-level entries with SSL ClientHello byte sequences (16 03 03, 16 03 02, 16 03 01, 16 03 00). The root cause is almost always the Azure Load Balancer health probe sending TCP or HTTPS probes to a HANA internal port that expects the native HANA replication protocol, not TLS.
symptoms: TrexNet error: 'new Request with no or invalid request begin identifier unsupported' on port 40006 or 30003
TrexNetBuffer error showing hex dump with 16 03 03 (TLS 1.2) or 16 03 01 (TLS 1.0) bytes
Erroneous SSL channel errors repeating every few seconds in nameserver alert trace
All connections are local (same host IP on both sides) or from the Azure LB probe IP
HANA processes otherwise running normally — no crash, no replication failure
investigation: Check nameserver_alert_<hostname>.trc for 'erroneous SSL channel' or 'TrexNet' errors
Identify the port number in the error — ports 3000x are instance ports, 4000x are internal
Check if the source IP matches the Azure LB probe IP (typically 168.63.129.16) or is localhost
Verify the Azure LB health probe configuration: az network lb probe show
Check if the probe is using TCP or HTTPS instead of the correct probe port (nc/socat)
Verify rsc_nc_<SID>_HDB<NR> resource is running (crm_mon) — this is the probe responder
root_cause: Azure Load Balancer health probe is configured to probe a HANA internal port (e.g. 40006) using TCP or HTTPS. HANA's internal TrexNet protocol does not understand TLS handshakes, causing repeated 'erroneous SSL channel' errors. The correct probe target should be the socat/nc listener port managed by the azure-lb Pacemaker resource.
fixes: Verify the Azure LB health probe targets the correct port — must match the port used by rsc_nc_<SID>_HDB<NR> (typically 625<NR>, e.g. 62500 for instance 00)
Do NOT probe HANA internal ports (30001-30007, 40001-40007) directly
If using a custom health probe, ensure it uses TCP on the socat/nc listener port, not HTTPS on a HANA port
Check Pacemaker resource rsc_nc_<SID>_HDB<NR> is Started — it runs the socat/nc process that responds to LB probes
Reference: SAP on Azure HA documentation for HANA load balancer configuration
